body.p: Claims 1-20 were and remain pending in the application. By this paper, claims 1 and 11 have been amended. No claims have been added or canceled. No new matter is added. Support for the amendments to the claims can be found, for example, in paragraph [0046] of the applicants' specification. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are hereby respectfully requested in view of the foregoing amendments and the following remarks.

Claims 1-3, 8, 10-13, 18, and 20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as obvious over U.S. Patent Document No. 2021/0383209 ("Brahma") in view of U.S. Patent No. 11,782,451 ("Venkatraman"). Claims 2, 3, 8, and 10 depend from claim 1. Claims 12, 18, and 20 depend from claim 11.
Claim 1, as amended, recites "a path generating device configured to generate
information on a first path for driving of an autonomous vehicle at an intersection based on map information[.]" Brahma and Venkatraman do not teach or suggest this limitation.
Brahma describes a method for training a model for an autonomous vehicle. See

Brahman, abstract; paragraph [0003]. Specifically, Brahma describes "a path planning system of the vehicle may determine, identify, generate, etc., a path for the vehicle based on objects detected by a perception system 1420 and estimated/predicted locations of the objects determined by the prediction system." See Brahma, paragraph [0083]. Accordingly, the path as described in Brahma is detected based on objects detected by a perception system of a vehicle and not map information. Thus, Brahma fails to teach or suggest the aforementioned limitation of claim 1 as amended.

Brahma further describes "a deviation in the path that exceeds a threshold deviation may indicate that the first neural network model is unable to process the image 1600 correctly (e.g., the first neural network has a bug and may be unable to generate a proper or correct path for the vehicle in certain conditions, instances, situations, etc.)." See Brahma, paragraph [0085]. The applicants further submit that the comparison as described in Brahma differs from the comparison of the present application, because the comparison in Brahma is for collection of an
image that a neural network model is unable to correctly process, whereas in the present disclosure, the comparison is for selectively learning the actual driving habits of a driver.

Venkatraman fails to cure the deficiencies of Brahma. Venkatraman is cited for path generation at an intersection. See Office action, page 4. Venkatraman is not cited for and does not teach or suggest the aforementioned limitations of independent claim 1.

For at least the foregoing reasons, the combination of Brahma and Venkatraman fails to teach or suggest one or more limitations of claim 1 as amended. Accordingly, amended claim 1 and corresponding dependent claims 2, 3, 8, and 10 are not rendered obvious by this cited reference combination.

Independent claim 11 has been amended to include limitations substantially similar to those of independent claim 1. For at least the same reasons as described above with respect to claim 1, the combination of Brahma and Venkatraman fails to teach or suggest one or more limitations of claim 11 as amended. Accordingly, amended claim 11 and corresponding dependent claims 12, 18, and 20 are not rendered obvious by the cited reference combination for consistent reasons.

Claims 4, 9, 14, and 19 are rejected as obvious over Brahma in view of Venkatraman and Chinese Patent Document No. CN 114184201 ("Xingjia"). Claims 4 and 9 depend from independent claim 1. Claims 14 and 19 depend from independent claim 11. The deficiencies in the teachings of Brahma and Venkatraman with respect to claims 1 and 11 are noted above. Xingjia fails to cure these deficiencies and has not been cited as doing so. Thus, the combination of Brahma, Venkatraman, and Xingjia fails to render obvious claims 1 and 11, and as a result, dependent claims 18 and 19 for at least the same reasons.

Claims 5-7 and 15-17 are rejected as obvious over Brahma in view of Venkatraman, U.S. Patent Publication No. 2022/0082403 ("Shapira"), and U.S. Patent Publication No. 2019/0071068 ("Shin"). Claims 5-7 depend from independent claim 1. Claims 15-17 depend from independent claim 11. The deficiencies in the teachings of Brahma and Venkatraman with respect to claims 1 and 11 are noted above. Shapira and Shin fail to cure these deficiencies and have not been cited as doing so. Thus, the combination of Brahma, Venkatraman, Shapira, and
Shin fails to render obvious claims 1 and 11, and as a result, dependent claims 5-7 and 15-17 for at least the same reasons.
The obviousness rejections are believed to be overcome.
Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are hereby respectfully solicited in view of the foregoing.

The examiner is invited to contact the undersigned at the telephone number listed below in order to discuss any remaining issues or matters of form that will place this case in condition for allowance.
No fee is believed due at this time.
